statement.p: The path C is a line segment of length 10 in the plane starting at (3,5). For f(x,y) = 6 x + 8 y, consider \int_C \nabla f \cdot d\vec r.
(a) Where should the other end of the line segment C be placed to maximize the value of the integral?
(b) What is the maximum value of the integral?

static.solution:
(a) To maximize the line integral, we choose C to be parallel to 
abla f= 6\vec i + 8\vec j. Thus C has parametric equation \vec r= (3\vec i+ 5\vec j) + t\vec v where \vec v= 6\vec i + 8\vec j, so x = 3 + 6 t \quad y= 5 + 8 t. If the other end of C is at (x_1,y_1), since the length of C is 10, we have \sqrt{(x_1 - 3)^2 + (y_1 - 5)^2} = 10, or \sqrt{(6 t)^2+(8 t)^2} = 10, so t\,\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = t\cdot 10 = 10. Thus t = 1 at (x_1,y_1), so x_1 = 3 + 1\cdot 6 = 9\quad\hbox{ and }\quad y_1 = 5 + 1\cdot 8 = 13, and C ends at the point (9,13).
(b) By the Fundamental Theorem of Line Integrals, \int_C 
abla f \cdot d\vec r = f(9,13) - f(3,5) =(6\cdot 9 + 8\cdot 13) - (6\cdot 3 + 8\cdot 5) = 100. Alternately, since 
abla f and C are parallel, \int_C 
abla f\cdot d\vec r = \Vert{
abla f}\Vert\cdot\hbox{Length of }C = 10 \cdot 10 = 100.
